main_text.l: cilii fancitum, fæpè faxo aut columnæ incidebant, & locis sacris figebant, interdum & jurejurando firmabant: à quo deinde recedere summum nefas ef-ferebantur. Vnde accidit aliquando,ut Romanos pro Lacedæmoniis quibus-dam intercedentes, contraque decretum tale aliquid enixius petentes, negando graviter offenderent: & cum Romani petitioni eidem nihilominus inhærerent, ac rationibus minas etiam adjicerent, cum summo dolore coge-rentur concedere, ut fixum petentes refigerent. Eveniebat porrò nonnun-quàm, ut soli urbium magistratus, non autem omnes, qui ad plenum juftumque concilium solent coire, convenirent: in quibus conventibus si quid decerneretur, quod non omnibus placeret, quodve primoribus quibusdam esset adversum, contra id tanquam non legitimum ac ratum ab iisdem excipiebatur. Quod quoties fiebat, necesse erat, in concilio proximo, ut ratum fieret, id ipsum refumi, ut vulgò loquimur, iterumque decerni. Notat etiam Polybius, cum caufa regum Ægypti au-lia contra Antiochum Syriæ regem [?]tentium ageretur paulò ante quàm

marginalia.note: Perseus Macedoniæ rex fuit captus, L. Æmilio Paulo [?], & C. Licinio Craslo [?] Romæ

page.notes: The marginal note on the left is partly cut off at the left edge of the scan. "Paulo ır" is read as "Paulo II" with doubt, and "Craflo" is read as "Craslo" (long s) with doubt; the last word of the note, "Romæ", is at the right of the note block. The left-margin reference marks (E-shaped) are not clearly tied to a word in the text, so the note is placed beside the line "[?]tentium", where it stands. The first word of the page "cilii" is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The leftmost word of the line "[?]tentium" is uncertain. "au-lia" is a line-end division that I could not confirm. The signature at the foot is a Greek-looking mark that I could not read letter by letter.
